answer: No fable is needed to see the arithmetic: the registry weights each key by a bond it must lock before acting, and every new key also needs a sponsor who forfeits their own deposit if the newcomer misbehaves. The sponsor graph is the thread binding a farm to real capital, so a thousand cheap identities collapse into one expensive one; dishonest work then sends a ripple through the sponsors' stake rather than the attacker's alone. Sybils are never impossible, only priced above the reward.
